newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares rise on hopes for rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares rise on hopes for rate cut.

text.p: Israeli shares closed higher in mixed and active trading on expectations the Bank of Israel will lower interest rates next week, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares gained 1.49 percent, or 0.76 points, to 196.59 on a high all-share turnover of 102 million shekels against 90 million on Monday.
The Maof 25 index rose 0.84 percent to 205.88.

"Activity was relatively high but the market is very nervous. The prices are very attractive but the redeployment of Syrian troops (in Lebanon) is worrying," said Ron Weisberg at I.B.I Investment House.
"The market expects the Bank of Israel will lower interest rates. The minimal rise of the money supply gives the central bank another reason to lower the rate," Weisberg said.
Israel's M1 money supply rose only 0.1 percent in August following a 4.1 percent rise in July.
Africa Israel Investments surged 6.0 percent to 411,697. Traders said the rise was a technical correction and that the share rose on very low volume.
Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, the third most active share, gained 4.0 percent to 135,706 on volume of 9.0 million shekels after its share traded on Nasdaq jumped 9.1 percent on Monday.

"Trading was very mixed today. The positive trend continues but we saw also some profit taking. Most of the activity was concentrated in the heavy stocks," said a trader at the First International Bank of Israel.
"The mood in the market is optimistic but investors are also very cautious. We are all waiting to see by how much the central bank will lower interest rates," he said.

The most active shares were Bezeq Israel Telecom, which gained 2.75 percent to 825 on volume of 11 million shekels and Koor Industries, which fell 0.25 percent to 28,367 on turnover of 10.4 million shekels.
